questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: being close to homecountry

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I liked living in Milan, but the school was very chaotic and lacked clear structure. Everyone was lost.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it a bit confusing, but good to have friends to help each other through it.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I went to Massimo's office. It was helpful. 

Went to an ECN introduction meeting, very confusing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were different campuses around Milan. I lived at Campus Martinitt, in the outer circle. It was 35 minutes away from Duomo (just for reference).

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: there was a bar that cooked food, but also one big kitchen for all 400+ students living at campus. Sometimes the kitchen was very dirty, other times things did not work. Around 20 o'clock it was too busy to get a stand to cook.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I very surprised that I needed to get a lot of stuff in order to just live normally. I needed to buy all kitchen supplies myself; pots and pans, knives, cutting board, cutlery, plates, bowls, glases, spices, just everything you can think of regarding cooking and eating.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was a nice area Lambrate. Cute to walk around in the small streets.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Assuming that 1 means least good. 

I was very difficult to get a propper schedule together with courses not overlapping.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
find courses before your arrival. 
check the schedule if they work together. 
register online at Ariel I think.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: you could contact Massimo. But everything had very little information, you were very much on your own.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: it worked out somewhat.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: prepare yourself mentally. accept that everything takes a long time, ask Massimo.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
it was different depending on which course. 
It was a lot of talking, no breaks, but at the same time little to no structure for most of the courses I attended.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
very different. I realised that I prefer home institution. 

there was just no structure and everything took a long time and little to no information. We didn't know where one exam to place until the day before. The day of the exam, the exam room changed.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Environmental and Food Law
Society, law and development 
Women in Tech
Gender Justice 
Economics of (organised) crime and corruption

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: economics of (organised) crime and corruption. Was the best course I had there, it was so different from the other courses, in the way of teaching and structure. Everything was very clear, the teacher was very interactive with students. Very good.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: the kitchen supplies mentioned earlier.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I was pretty much what I thought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not attend. I paid for an ESN card, but was not worth.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know. Other than ESN.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: just explore with friends, there are many thing to do and see in Milan. I enjoyed an art-course down by Navgli, but it was a bit expensive.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go on short tips to the cities around Milan. Bergamo, Como, Firenze.. lots to see, easy with train. 
Sometimes it can take the same amount of time to get to the other end of the Milan circle, as it takes to go to Bergamo.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I thought it was quite easy, my "problem" was mostly adjusting to how unorganised the school is and all the practical stuff regarding that.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: speak with them in class or go see something by night.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: mostly the "loose" structure

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: how open some people were. Very nice people, good and cheap food. I liked the "calmness" and just to explore the city on my own or with friends. Milan has many great restaurants, bars and cafes.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Prepare mentally for all the practical stuff.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: don't stress over the practical stuff, it is just how it is.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: meeting new friends, and just the indepence and insight in the culture and way of living.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: the pratical stuff.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
